Y'all have seen me talk about this — here's where it's at.

30+ years with Type 1 Diabetes. My daughter diagnosed at 3. A car wreck from a low on my way to work. All of it led me to build @avatype1.

🎮 App that makes learning about diabetes fun for kids
🚗 Device that shows your BG on your dashboard while driving
💊 Free tools to find financial help for insulin & supplies

Check it out: https://ava-type1.github.io

T1D fam — I'd love feedback. Shares help too 💙

#Type1Diabetes #T1D #DiabetesAwareness #AVAType1

I was diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes at age 4. That was 1992.

In 2022, my daughter Kaislyn was diagnosed at age 3.

30 years apart. Same disease. Same fear.

But this time, I could do something about it.

Today I'm launching AVA Type 1. 🧵

posts.content:
AVA Type 1 is a simulation game that teaches kids ages 5-18 how to manage Type 1 Diabetes.

Carb counting. Insulin dosing. Recognizing highs and lows.

Not a textbook. A game.

Because kids learn by playing, not by reading pamphlets in a doctor's office.

I built this with SwiftUI on nights and weekends. No VC funding. No team of 50. Just a dad who's lived with T1D for 30+ years and a daughter who deserves better tools than I had.

Every feature comes from real experience. Not focus groups.

And we're building something physical too — AVA Buddy.

A plush companion with an ESP32 display that connects to the app via Bluetooth. Something a kid can hold. Something that makes diabetes feel less lonely.

Coming soon.

If you know a kid with T1D, a newly diagnosed family, a school nurse, an endo — share this.

AVA Type 1 is on the App Store now.

Making learning about diabetes care feel less like a burden and more like an adventure.

@avatype1 🩵

To every parent who's set a 2AM alarm to check blood sugar:

Hook: "'Can't you just give her less sugar?'" (deadpan stare)

Rapid-fire myth-busting. "Type 1 is autoimmune, not dietary." "No, she didn't eat too much candy." "Yes, she will have this forever." "No, cinnamon won't fix it." End: "This is why I built an app — because education matters."

posts.content:
Quick T1D fact most people don't know:

Type 1 is autoimmune. The body attacks its own insulin-producing cells. It has nothing to do with diet or lifestyle.

You can't prevent it. You can't reverse it. You manage it. Every single day.

Hook: "I asked my daughter to explain her diabetes."

posts.content:
The T1D community is the most resilient group of people I've ever known.

30 years in, and I'm still learning from you.

Building @avatype1 in the open because this community deserves transparency, not marketing.

Hot take: Most diabetes education materials are designed for adults and handed to children.

Kids deserve tools built *for* them. Not adapted *at* them.
